Maria (SRE): Heads-up — we've been getting a bunch of pager churn from short-lived GPU metric spikes. Can we rethink paging so operators only get paged for signals that look like real incidents, not telemetry noise?

Ajay (SRE): 100%. A lot of the pages last week were sub-2min flares where autoscaling or cache warmup resolved things. We should separate transient spikes from sustained/causal failures.

Maria (SRE): Proposed pattern: two-layer alerting + contextual routing.
- Tier A: high-confidence pages — sustained high util, OOMs, node_down, daemon crashes, service errors correlated with GPU failures.
- Tier B: noisy metric spikes — open a ticket (low priority) + create an aggregated alert for engineers to review.

Taylor (EngOps): How do we avoid missing capacity problems during bursts? e.g. many pools at ~75% but none individually hit page thresholds.

Ajay (SRE): Keep a pool-saturation page rule: `gpu_pool_sustained_utilization` > 75% for 10m -> page. Spikes (p95/p99) -> ticket after short `for` window. Also add an auto-escalation: if tickets of the same alert exceed N in M minutes, promote to page.

Leo (Infra): Add cost/tenant context: Dedicated/Reserved capacity customers get faster paging (SLA) even on smaller signals; hosted/batch tenants get ticket-first behavior. We can route by `customer_tier` label.

Maria (SRE): Example Prometheus alert rules (prototype):
```yaml
- alert: GPUPoolSustainedHighUtil
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_pool_utilization[10m]) > 0.75
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
    category: capacity
  annotations:
    runbook: https://wiki.redwood/infrastructure/runbooks/gpu-capacity
    summary: "Sustained GPU pool saturation (>75% for 10m)"

- alert: GPUUtilSpike
  expr: increase(gpu_utilization[2m]) > 0.30
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
    category: noisy_metric
  annotations:
    summary: "Short spike in GPU utilization (ticket)"
```

Maria (SRE): And Alertmanager routes: route by `severity` label — `page` -> oncall pager; `ticket` -> ticketing webhook + ops-channel. For `ticket`, attach a short dedup window and grouping by `pool` to avoid one-ticket-per-node storms.

OncallBot: [alert] GPUUtilSpike fired for pool=eu-west-1-gpu-1 (auto-ingest)

Ajay (SRE): Operational rules to reduce fatigue:
- Debounce: if identical alert fires >3 times in 15m, suppress further pages and escalate to an aggregated ticket.
- Auto-snooze: after a page for the same `pool` we mute similar severity=page alerts for 10m unless the alert's annotations indicate `oom` or `node_down`.
- Manual override: allow oncall to unmute if they want continuous paging.

Taylor (EngOps): Need metrics to measure impact: page_rate / ticket_rate per pool, avg time operator is paged, % tickets auto-promoted. We'll add these to SLO dashboards.

Leo (Infra): I'll add an Alertmanager route that uses `customer_tier` + `severity` to decide paging and will implement dedup keys. Also will create a Grafana panel for "page vs ticket churn" and a small SLO for pages/day per oncall.

Ajay (SRE): Also include `trace_id` / `last_log_link` annotations so triage is faster — small improvement reduces time-to-diagnose and makes tickets less noisy.

Maria (SRE): Agreed. I'll draft the PR for the rule changes and the runbook update. Targeting staging tests next week.

Leo (Infra): I'll carve out time to wire the routes and dashboard. Ping me if you want pair-testing.

Taylor (EngOps): :thumbsup: Good plan. Once PR is up we'll run a small chaos simulation (simulate repeated spikes) to validate auto-snooze and escalation behavior.

Maria (SRE): Thanks everyone — hoping this reduces midnight pagers and improves signal quality for real incidents.

Leo (Infra): Follow-up: I'll post the PR link here once ready.
